newsitem.title: USA: Fed expected to add reserves via system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed expected to add reserves via system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to add temporary reserves to the banking system through multi-day system repurchases on Thursday, analysts said.

"We're calling for a seven-day system RP," said Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities America Inc. "(Federal) funds are comfortable," he said, referring to the fact that Fed funds were trading at the Fed's target rate of 5-1/2 percent, "but it's a new maintenance period and the Fed has to get reserves into the banking system.
"They have nothing in there right now and they probably want to keep pace with the reserve need," said Moran.
Moran said he calculated the Fed's daily reserve need at $3.5 billion a day for the new two-week maintenance period which he said was "not large."
Patricia Thrapp, vice president at Aubrey G. Lanston & Co, said she expected the Fed to add reserves through four-day fixed system repurchase agreements.
Thrapp said she calculated the Fed's daily add need at $2.0 billion during the first week of the two-week bank reserve maintenance period rising to $3.0 billion a day in the second week.
At 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, the Federal funds rate was quoted at 5-1/2 percent, the Fed's target for the rate.
